key_insight: The paper introduces a scalable method to make Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) for load forecasting explainable by computing SHAP attributions that incorporate covariates, enabling transparent, trustworthy forecasts for power systems.
problem_solved: Black-box TSFMs provide strong forecasting performance but lack transparency needed for critical infrastructure (e.g., power grids). The paper addresses the need for efficient, faithful feature-attribution explanations tailored to covariate-informed TSFMs used in load forecasting.
method: Design an efficient algorithm to compute SHAP-style attributions specifically adapted to TSFMs that use time-varying covariates and long context windows.
Exploit model and data structure (covariate conditioning, temporal decomposition) to reduce computation compared to naive SHAP, making explanations scalable to real-world load datasets.
Validate the approach on covariate-informed load forecasting tasks to demonstrate faithful, interpretable attributions while preserving forecasting accuracy.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to open the black box of TSFMs in energy applications, improving trust, diagnostics, and decision support for grid operators without sacrificing scalability. It bridges state-of-the-art forecasting with actionable explainability.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: TSFM model + covariates → efficient SHAP module → time-resolved attributions

Bar/heatmap: feature importance ranking across forecasting horizons or regions
Icon set: power grid, clock/time series, magnifying glass (explainability), speedometer (efficiency/scalability)
paper_title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
paper_authors: Matthias Hertel, Alexandra Nikoltchovska, Sebastian Pütz, Ralf Mikut, Benjamin Schäfer
